brief_item.title: ECLoop用仓库证据门控阻止编码Agent过早提交
brief_item.core_conclusion: ECLoop把任务要求编译成可核验的仓库证据条件，依据AST、调用图和类层次绑定实体，再按工具事件维护证据缺口。编辑与提交在条件满足前暂停，减少编码Agent过早改动。
brief_item.mechanism: 运行时记录Read、Grep、测试及其输出，分别判断全局与动作级证据是否齐备。信息收集可自由执行，编辑或提交触发缺口检查，未满足时返回缺失证据并重试，最多三次后进入审计回退。
brief_item.result: 在500个SWE-bench Verified实例上，ECLoop让两个模型、两种Agent脚手架的Pass@1提升4.8至11.8个百分点，平均Token用量下降1.4%至12.1%，推理成本下降1.5%至10.2%。
brief_item.boundary: 收益来自软件修复基准，不能直接外推到其他仓库、任务或模型。证据规范可能遗漏难以落地的条件，三次暂停后仍可审计放行，覆盖率和安全性取决于领域谓词。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可在运行时保留Read、Grep探索自由，同时要求调用方、测试和失败条件形成可观测证据后才允许修改。把任务完整性放到模型外，并为较弱Agent设置审计回退。

facts.title: Preventing Premature Commitment in Coding Agents with an Evidence-Conditioned Execution Layer
facts.event_hint: ECLoop gates coding-agent edits and submissions on deterministically checked repository evidence
facts.problem: Coding agents can edit code or submit patches before inspecting callers, related implementations, tests, or failure conditions that would justify the commitment. Prompt-only guidance cannot verify that required evidence was actually gathered.
facts.mechanism: ECLoop compiles task-specific evidence conditions from the issue and repository structure, grounds them to concrete entities using AST/call-graph/class-hierarchy analysis, observes runtime commands and outputs as structured events, and maintains global and action-specific evidence gaps. Information-gathering actions proceed freely; edits and submissions are held until their relevant conditions are satisfied, with missing evidence returned as guidance.

evidence.claim: Across all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, ECLoop improved Pass@1 by 4.8–11.8 percentage points across two language models and two agent scaffolds.
evidence.baseline: same model, prompt, tools, and scaffold without ECLoop
evidence.condition: 500 SWE-bench Verified instances; MiniMax-M2.5 and GPT-5-mini; mini-swe-agent v2 and Codex CLI
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.1 Abstract; p.2 evaluation summary

evidence.claim: Under mini-swe-agent v2, Pass@1 rose from 56.2% to 68.0% for GPT-5-mini and from 75.8% to 80.6% for MiniMax-M2.5.
ECLoop reduced average token usage by 1.4–12.1% and inference cost by 1.5–10.2% across the four model–scaffold configurations.
A commitment action is postponed when its action-specific evidence gap is nonempty; the system retries the same target up to three times before an audited fallback allows it to proceed.
evidence.condition: source-code edit or final submission with unsatisfied conditions
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.5 Section 3.3 Execution control and guarantees

evidence.claim: Evidence satisfaction is computed deterministically from recorded repository observations and tool outputs rather than from the model claiming that it completed an investigation.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.4 Section 3.1 Formal evidence representation; Section 3.2

facts.evaluation_context: The paper evaluates ECLoop on all 500 SWE-bench Verified issues using MiniMax-M2.5 and GPT-5-mini with mini-swe-agent v2 and OpenAI Codex CLI. Baseline and ECLoop runs share model, prompt, tools, and scaffold; only the evidence-conditioned execution layer differs.
facts.limitations: The paper studies software repair and notes that applying ECLoop elsewhere requires domain-specific evidence representations and satisfaction procedures. Generated evidence specifications can omit checks when conditions cannot be grounded, reducing coverage. After the three-hold budget, an audited fallback may still execute an unsupported commitment. The benchmark does not establish behavior on other repositories, tasks, or agent models.
facts.project_relevance: This is directly relevant to preventing premature code edits: a runtime layer can preserve free-form Read/Grep exploration while blocking edits until callers, tests, or other required evidence are observed. It suggests enforcing task integrity outside the model, with an explicit fallback audit rather than relying on weaker agents to self-police.
